institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academically I am specifically interested in The Nordic and Arctic region in terms of security. Thus, UiT The Arctic University of Norway was a perfect choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Socially and regionally found it to be very giving and exciting. The academic level felt a bit lower than what I am used to at home,.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit of a long process, but I assume that is to be expected. Both UiT and KU were fairly helpful in sharing information and assisting in confusion.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None really. Apart from introduction meetings about the university in general. I had already found housing when I arrived and had been in contact with my study advisor about various communal activities for my partner, who came along with me and our baby.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation itself could have been more informative, but it did not affect my situation a lot since I had researched and figured out a lot of things at home prior to arrival. Apart from this, there was not a lot of social erasmus gatherings at the university either. We were several students who talked about this - there were events for erasmus students held other places both in public and in private, but not very many gatherings AT the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My partner and I found housing through a Facebook group. In our situation it was was quite easy, perhaps because we started looking for housing very early due to our situation with bringing along our baby.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's usually a bit more expensive but gives you the benefit of living elsewhere in the area and thus (perhaps) connecting with the local community. This was our experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was never something we considered for our situation, so it is a bit hard for me to rate.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In my case it was quite intuitive. I ended up attending a "package deal" meaning I followed courses that were all mandatory to one specific education at the university. This meant, that all exams, presentations etc. were planned out properly and never overlapped.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At first, it took some time understanding the concept of choosing a "package" of courses. But once I figured it out, it was an easy process and it was quickly accepted, since all timetables for the courses were already planned out in advance. I simply followed an already-set semester structure.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online webinars and emails prior to the arrival. There was no phone number to call which - at one point in the process - was frustrating, because the responding time on emails was long at times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, since I was quickly accepted for the package semester deal, I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to carefully choose and consider if they overlap in exam periods. If possible in any way, I would definitely consider choosing a package semester deal, since it makes it easier for you work and time wise. Another benefit of this is also, that you follow the same group of people for the whole semester, which is really nice socially.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay, but the overall teaching level felt lower than from what I am used to at my master's degree back home. I definitely learned new things academically, but the learning curve did not feel as steep as I am used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two courses in total. One big 20-ects course and one smaller 10-ects class. The big one was a bit dissappointing in its academic level. We had constant changes in teachers and thus teaching methods. Although this can also have benefits, it also contributed to a lot of confusion for the students. Many of the teachers' learning outcomes did not correspond. The subjects and themes interested me a whole lot, but the teaching methods and the teachers made it difficult. Some teachers' (low) level of english pronounciation also made it difficult to follow along at times.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar in the sense that it was highly based on participatory teaching methods. But as I have described above, the overall level was lower.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
(SVF-3021) Integrated Peace and Conflict Studes 

(SVF-3022) Culture, Conflict and Society

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Culture, Conflict and Society. This course only had 1 teacher and it was well put together, with a good mixture of assignments, preseantations and lectures. The length was only 1,5 months, and the intensity of the course made it constantly interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expensive groceries and expensive tourist bookings. I don't know if this was unexpected, but it is important to keep in mind. Especially groceries is important to budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were. But local transportation was quite cheap, which was important! In general I would recommend talking to locals about opportunities and recommendations for experiences, trips and rental stuff. This helped us out a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I personally attended a choir and a gym at the university, and was very satisfied with both. Other than this, the university offered a lot of different clubs and teams to join. In reality, a lot more than from what I am used to at KU.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to the university gym, KRAFT and sang in a student choir. Especially with the choir, I had really nice experiences with singing jobs and social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Since I did not join a sports team, I can't recommend that. But my partner played at the ice hockey team, and had a great experience with that. 
On the other hand I can really recommend joining the choir, if one is into singing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Pust sauna at the harbour. 
Renting a car cheap through local services and driving out in nature. 
Sleeping in tents out in nature 
Joining social activities for exchange students

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - we could communicate with the local people in Danish/Norwegian, and the culture was in many ways similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Trying to learn just a few basic sentences in Norwegian and being curious. Another thing is to join a local sports team, since this can give you the opportunity to get to know locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. There were indeed small differences in culture than from what I am used to - but none that I found challenging as a Dane.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendlyness and the open-minded attitude. We met so many nice local people, who gave us recommendations and tips for living in the cold.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be into outdoor activities 
Bring suitable clothes for the weather
Engage with the local community

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I described a lot of things in the previous, but overall it is to engage not only with other excahnge students but also with local people if poosible. At least to be curious.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature experience was definitely one of the most rewarding experiences. This, and getting a deeper understanding of the the challenges in the Arctic region.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The heavy snow and (at times) quite extreme weather. But this was also one of the most special experiences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
